items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: run by Stanley Cowell, the father of Stanley Cowell, the pianist.

ctx.x: You must have – what is it? I want to say a photogenic [sic] memory, but it’s not that – but when you hear something, it seems to be captured. For instance, I don’t know what – how did you work in the early days? When it – since there were tapes and there were albums, but I couldn’t imagine that you always had an album to work from or a tape to work from.

Oh, no. I would work from what I heard. I would hear something. Like I used to make money to go to the movies. The movies was a dime. Popcorn was a nickel. So I would go to the local hamburger joint, Stanley’s Hamburgers, run by Stanley Cowell, the father of Stanley Cowell, the pianist.
